title: Adding Lucene-style ?q= query string search for alerts made the Postgres backend build WHERE clauses by str.format()-ing user search terms into SQL.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: User‑controlled query string (params['q']) is parsed and then interpolated directly into SQL fragments via __repr__ methods (e.g., "'{}' ILIKE '%%{}%%'".format(self.tokens.field, self.tokens.word)). No parameter binding or strict allow‑listing is applied, enabling injection of arbitrary SQL.

findings.suggested_fix: Replace string interpolation with parameterized queries. Build the SQL using placeholders (e.g., %s) and pass user values to the DB driver separately, or use an ORM query builder that safely escapes values. Also validate/allowlist allowed fields and operators before constructing the query.

findings.explanation: The changes only add parsing logic for search expressions and do not modify any endpoint, resource lookup, or authorization checks. No new object‑ID handling or protected operation is introduced.
